case_name: Sandeep Kumar vs Of on 9 January, 2024

parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Rajni Kumari & another — wife and another person

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner's wife started beating him, demanding money to purchase a car. He gave beatings to her on 23.11.2020 in the presence of her mother. Petitioner filed a complaint before SHO, Women Police Station and a case under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act was registered.

legal_principles.principle: A wife has a reasonable cause to reside separately from her husband and claim maintenance where there is a reasonable apprehension in the mind of the wife that she would be physically harmed.
legal_principles.held: It was observed: A clear perusal of this provision manifestly shows that it was meant to give a clear instance of circumstances which may be treated as a just ground for the refusal of the wife to live with her husband.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005
cited_cases: Sirajmohmedkhan Versus Hafizunnisa Yasinkhan AIR 1981 Supreme Court 1972

legal_principles.principle: A court must consider the plea taken by a respondent that the petitioner is residing separately without any reasonable cause and there is no justification for granting maintenance.
legal_principles.held: The learned Principal Judge, Family Court did not of consider the plea taken by the respondent that petitioner no.1 is residing separately from the respondent without any reasonable cause and there is no justification for grating the maintenance.

outcome.final_order: Interim maintenance of ₹5000/- was granted to respondent no. 1 (petitioner's wife) and ₹1500/- to respondent no. 2 from the date of filing of the application.
